ntwine mark

Every candidate is three strands laid along one centreline, with exact crossings and a real over/under. Each row: the 512 art at 256 and 180, then 32 and 16 rasterized and upscaled with nearest-neighbour, then the 16 and 32 at true size on light and dark tab strips. Rebuild with nub assets/logo-ntwine/concepts.ts.

The mark

Three threads come in, plait through three crossings, and leave as three. Installed as the app icon, the site's icons and hero, the social card and the VS Code activity bar.

Alone and one-colour

The mark without its tile (social card, site hero), and the line-art version VS Code paints as a mask, at 16 and 24px.

Round one: twelve directions, gaps as round-capped cuts

Plaits, ropes, rings and an n. Cutting the under strand and capping the cut round turned every weave into a row of separate noodles, and at a shallow crossing the cut ran so long that little of a strand was left. The rope ring is too close to OpenAI's mark. Nothing here reads as entwined threads at 16px.

Round two: woven gaps

The gap is now a mask drawn along the strand on TOP, so its edges run parallel to that strand, the way a woven ribbon is drawn. Every weave became legible at 180 and above. The plait reads as a braid; the rope as rope or DNA; three exact circles as Borromean rings, which are entwined but are rings, not threads. The n built from strands is a good arch at 16px and a tangle at 512.

Round three: the plait, tuned for 16px

Fewer, larger crossings keep a zigzag at 16px. A bleeding plait is the strongest picture inside the tile, but the mark also has to stand alone — the VS Code activity bar, the site's hero, the social card — and a plait that runs off the edge has nothing to end on there. It also puts ink outside the maskable icon's safe circle.

Round four: a contained plait, and how it ends

Loose threads at both ends: three threads come in, plait, and leave as three — the brief's n threads, entwined. Three crossings is the fewest that still reads as a plait and the only count whose two big X's survive 16px. A spindle (gathered to points) reads as a leaf or a flame.

Round five: three crossings, pen, gap and ramp

Wider gaps (about 0.7px at 16px) beat a heavier pen. A short ramp (40) leaves a visible corner where a tail meets the weave; a long one (96) does not. Easing the amplitude into the tails merges the threads into a blob. Three golds read beautifully at 512 and add noise at 16; one gold matches the shipped tile. The final mark is 5a's geometry, scaled to a 404-unit ink height.
